data.narrative:
Aclarity is a Series A climate and energy company founded by Julie Bliss Mullen that has raised $14M to date. The valuation analysis draws on a sector universe of 9 private climate and energy firms—including peers such as Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen—plus one public comparable (LNZA).

A peer-median approach was not feasible due to insufficient same-stage or adjacent-stage comparables within the narrow Climate & Energy category; only one applicable triangulation method was executable. The stage-progression method applies a 2.0x step-up multiplier from Aclarity's $14M total raised as a valuation proxy, implying a post-Series A value of $28M. This reflects typical Series A → next-stage expansion multiples observed in venture-backed companies at equivalent developmental stages.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $24M to $32M, with a median point of $28M. This range reflects the tension between using only total capital raised as an anchor (a backward-looking, conservative proxy) and the typical dilution and step-up seen between financing rounds. Key uncertainties include the absence of tight peer multiples at identical stage and valuation bands, which limits confidence in calibration. A more precise valuation would benefit from operational metrics, market traction data, and a larger set of same-stage Climate & Energy comparables.
